review_notes:
I read all of Center.lean (lines 1–130). I then searched the repo for other uses of coordinateRotation and coordinateHalfTurn. Those are in CoordinateRotation.lean, AlgebraicGroup/SpecialOrthogonal/Irreducible.lean and AlgebraicGroup/SpecialOrthogonal/Center.lean. I also searched for other centrality, Commute and scalar-orthogonal arguments.

Irreducible.lean uses half-turns to show an invariant subspace contains a basis vector. That is a different argument from the one here, which shows a commuting matrix is scalar.

AlgebraicGroup/SpecialOrthogonal/Center.lean only wraps this file's results. It does not repeat their proofs. The sq_eq_one_of_smul_one_mem_orthogonalGroup lemma is already shared, and StandardComodule.lean uses it too.

Inside the target, `hoff` and `hdiag` both apply `Commute` to a `Pi.single` vector and read off one coordinate. This is only a short repeated pattern, and the two calculations differ in the rotation used and in the algebra that follows. Extracting a helper would just move the repetition. I found no repeated argument that justifies a shared lemma. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out subtler overlap elsewhere in the repo.
